title: Online IB Biology Tutoring SL & HL | Auxesis Education
description: Individualized online IB Biology tutoring for SL and HL, including conceptual understanding, exam preparation and ethical IA guidance.
heading: Online IB Biology tutoring
intro: Master IB Biology by connecting the microscopic world of cells and molecules with the physiological processes that sustain life. Using interactive models, visual simulations and carefully chosen examples, I help students make sense of complex biological systems and see how ideas fit together across the SL and HL curriculum.
sections: Unity and Diversity

Explore the remarkable diversity of life while uncovering the fundamental biological principles that unite living organisms. From molecular structures and cell organization to classification and evolutionary relationships, I use interactive models, visual comparisons and scientific evidence to help students recognize patterns and connections. Together, we develop the analytical skills needed to interpret unfamiliar biological examples, compare organisms and construct precise, evidence-based examination responses.
Form and Function

Understanding the relationship between biological structure and function is central to IB Biology. Students explore how molecular structures, cell organization and specialized tissues enable living systems to function. Through interactive visualizations and guided analysis, I help students connect structures with their biological roles, interpret unfamiliar diagrams and apply these principles to challenging examination questions. A common difficulty is explaining how a particular structure makes a process possible, rather than identifying its parts. We use labelled diagrams and questions to build the connection step by step.
Interaction and Interdependence

Discover the intricate relationships that connect organisms, biological systems and their environments. From cellular communication and physiological regulation to ecological interactions and energy flow, I help students decode complex biological processes through visual simulations, interconnected models and real-world examples. We develop the scientific reasoning needed to interpret experimental data, explain biological interactions and apply knowledge across multiple levels of organization. When a pathway feels like a collection of disconnected steps, we trace the inputs, changes and outputs together before applying the model to an unfamiliar example.
Continuity and Change

Unravel the mechanisms that maintain life across generations while driving biological change. From DNA replication and inheritance to natural selection, evolution and biodiversity, I guide students through the molecular and evolutionary processes that shape living systems. Using genetic models, data analysis and structured problem-solving, we transform abstract concepts into clear scientific explanations, building the precision needed to evaluate evidence and tackle challenging IB examination questions.
Understanding and examination technique

We work through unfamiliar diagrams, experimental data and challenging questions, building understanding rather than relying on memorized answers. I also teach students to decode command terms and dissect mark schemes, so they can turn sound biological knowledge into clear, precise examination responses. The aim is greater confidence, stronger scientific reasoning and a deeper understanding of Biology. Lessons use the student’s classroom work and upcoming assessments; we can rebuild foundations or focus on greater precision in applying and communicating ideas.
Can you help with a Biology IA or Extended Essay?

Yes. I provide ethical guidance for Biology Internal Assessments and Extended Essays, helping students think through questions, methods, analysis and evaluation. The decisions, analysis and final submitted work remain the student’s own.
Do you support both SL and HL Biology?
Yes. Lessons are tailored to the student’s level, course requirements and questions, whether the priority is a difficult topic, ongoing understanding or examination preparation.
An experienced teacher
My experience includes international classroom teaching and work as an IB Biology Assistant Examiner, including Internal Assessment moderation.

title: Online IB Chemistry Tutoring SL & HL | Auxesis Education
description: Online one-to-one IB Chemistry tutoring for SL and HL, with conceptual explanations, problem-solving, exam preparation and ethical IA guidance.
heading: Online IB Chemistry tutoring
intro: Master IB Chemistry by decoding chemical structure, reactivity and the principles governing chemical systems. Through interactive models, visual simulations and worked examples, I help students visualize abstract reactions and connect particle-level explanations with observable changes.
sections: Structure: models, bonding and materials

We explore the particulate nature of matter, atomic structure, bonding and the organization of substances. Visual models help students connect electron arrangements and bonding to the properties of materials, while calculations and evidence help them test and communicate their explanations. Students can find it difficult to move between a particle model, a formula and a bulk property; we compare representations and explain the link rather than treating each as a separate fact.
Reactivity: energy, rates and chemical change

We investigate why and how chemical reactions occur, including energy changes, reaction rates and equilibrium, acids and bases, redox and relevant organic reactions. Simulations and worked examples help students connect equations, mechanisms and particle-level models to observations and solve unfamiliar problems. For example, an equilibrium model can help distinguish equal reaction rates from equal concentrations and explain how a system responds to a change in conditions.
Calculations, practical work and evidence

We work through the reasoning behind quantities, units and multi-step calculations, checking whether an answer is chemically sensible. Students also practise interpreting experimental results, evaluating methods and connecting evidence with explanations. Lessons are shaped by the student’s classroom work and the areas where understanding or application is getting in the way.
From understanding to examination responses

Lessons follow the SL or HL curriculum and develop the confidence to move between equations, models, experimental evidence and scientific explanations. We explore the reasoning behind calculations, reaction mechanisms and unfamiliar problems, rather than simply memorizing procedures. Students learn to interpret command terms, dissect mark schemes and structure answers with precision. We practise with unfamiliar questions, identifying what the question asks, selecting the relevant chemistry and showing a clear chain of reasoning.
Building connections across the course

Chemical ideas are more useful when students can connect them. We revisit prerequisite concepts where needed and link Structure and Reactivity through examples from the student’s course, so that bonding, energy and particle behaviour support rather than compete with one another.
Can you help with the Chemistry Internal Assessment?
Yes. Guidance can support planning, interpretation and evaluation while protecting academic integrity: the student makes the decisions and produces their own analysis and final submitted work.
Do you teach both SL and HL Chemistry?
Yes. Lessons follow the student’s level and course, whether they need support with foundational ideas, HL material, calculations or examination preparation.

title: GCSE & IGCSE Biology and Chemistry Tutoring | Auxesis
description: Online GCSE and IGCSE Biology and Chemistry tutoring, including Biology and Chemistry components of Combined Science and preparation for further study.
heading: GCSE and IGCSE science tutoring
intro: Build confidence in GCSE and IGCSE Biology and Chemistry through clear teaching that connects scientific ideas with practical application. I guide students through biological systems, chemical reactions and the principles that link topics together, using interactive models, visual explanations and targeted problem-solving.
sections: Biology: from cells to living systems

We explore topics such as cell structure, movement of substances, human physiology, inheritance and ecology, as relevant to the student’s specification. Visual models and comparisons help students connect structures to their functions and explain processes instead of learning isolated facts. Students may know the names of structures yet find it difficult to explain how they work; we use diagrams and familiar examples to make the relationship clear.
Chemistry: particles, reactions and calculations

Lessons can cover atomic structure, bonding, the periodic table, reactions and quantitative chemistry, according to the examination board. We use particle models, equations and worked examples to connect what happens in a reaction with observations and calculations. When balancing equations or working with moles, we trace the meaning of each symbol and step, then practise applying the same reasoning to a new question.
Practical science, data and explanations

We work with the investigations and practical skills in the student’s course: interpreting graphs, considering variables, describing patterns and using evidence to support a conclusion. Questions help us check whether understanding holds when it has to be applied, not simply recalled.
Building a stronger foundation

A student may need to revisit an earlier topic, prepare for an assessment or gain confidence with a new school course. We use class materials and upcoming assessments to decide where to begin, then connect ideas across Biology and Chemistry at the appropriate level.
Lessons matched to the examination board

Lessons follow the student’s examination board and specification, including the Biology and Chemistry components of Combined or Coordinated Science. We identify gaps in understanding, practise interpreting data and develop the skills needed to tackle unfamiliar questions. Students also learn to decode command terms and dissect mark schemes, turning scientific knowledge into well-structured examination answers.
Does Combined or Coordinated Science support include Physics?

Support covers the Biology and Chemistry components only. Courses differ by examination board, so please share the specification or topics when enquiring and I can confirm whether the support is suitable.
Can tutoring help with the transition to IB or A-Level?

Yes. Students can strengthen foundations before or during GCSE or IGCSE, then revisit key ideas before moving to IB Biology, IB Chemistry or AS and A-Level Biology. The pathway and support depend on the student’s goals.
Experienced science teaching
My international classroom experience includes teaching GCSE and IGCSE Biology and Chemistry.

title: Online AS & A-Level Biology Tutoring | Auxesis Education
description: Online AS and A-Level Biology tutoring for understanding advanced concepts, interpreting data and preparing for examinations.
heading: Online AS and A-Level Biology tutoring
intro: Develop a deeper understanding of AS and A-Level Biology through teaching that brings advanced biological concepts into focus. I guide students through molecular processes, physiological systems and the connections between topics, using interactive models, visual simulations and structured problem-solving.
sections: Molecules, cells and genetic information

We explore biological molecules, enzymes, cell structure, membranes and the flow of genetic information, as appropriate to the student’s specification. Visual models help students trace processes such as gene expression and connect molecular events to their biological consequences. Students can struggle to keep track of where a process happens and how its stages connect; we map each step and explain the role of the molecules involved.
Physiology, energy and living systems

Students can examine topics such as transport, exchange, respiration, photosynthesis and regulation. I use diagrams, simulations and guided questions to connect mechanisms across cells, tissues and whole organisms, rather than treating each topic in isolation. For example, we can use a model of a membrane to connect transport at the cellular level with exchange across an organ system.
Inheritance, evolution and ecology

Where included in the course, we work through inheritance, genetic variation, natural selection and ecosystems. Genetic models and data analysis help students explain patterns, evaluate evidence and apply biological principles in unfamiliar contexts.
Practical work and data analysis

We examine the purpose and design of investigations, the choice of variables, the presentation of data and the strength of conclusions. I guide students through unfamiliar graphs and practical contexts so they can distinguish an observation from an inference and support their reasoning with evidence.
Scientific evidence and examination technique

Lessons follow the student’s examination board and specification, with particular attention to experimental evidence, data interpretation and the demanding synoptic questions that require knowledge from across the course. We work on explaining mechanisms accurately, evaluating conclusions and applying ideas in unfamiliar contexts. By decoding command terms and dissecting mark schemes, students learn to construct precise, well-reasoned answers. Synoptic questions can be demanding because the relevant ideas are drawn from different parts of the course; we practise identifying those links and selecting only the knowledge needed to answer.
Can you help students interpret practical work and data?
Yes. We can examine experimental design, graphs and results, evaluate conclusions and practise explaining the evidence in the context of the student’s course.
Experience across curricula
My international classroom experience includes teaching AS and A-Level Biology.
